title: Exact ringed pullback identifies the canonical signed derived tensor comparison
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,R)$ and $(\mathcal D,S)$ be ringed sites small relative to a common universe of ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ be a geometric morphism of their sheaf topoi, with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits and a map of commutative ring sheaves $u^{-1}R\to S$. The module pullback $F(M)=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$ uses [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; assume $F$ exact. Use the unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the actual K-flat derived tensors [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and the canonical left derived pullback $L=Lu^*$ with its resolving-model comparison $e_E:L(q_RE)\cong q_S(FE)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Let $U=D(F)$ be localization of termwise $F$, with factorization $\kappa_E:U(q_RE)\cong q_S(FE)$.

There is a unique natural isomorphism $\eta:L\xrightarrow{\sim}U$ with $\kappa_E\eta_{q_RE}=e_E$ for every flat-term K-flat $E$. It respects all integer shift comparisons and the degree-zero sheaf comparisons. Module pullback preserves flat sheaves and flat-term K-flat complexes [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex].

Transport along $\eta$ the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $\mu_{K,H}:U(K\otimes_R^LH)\cong UK\otimes_S^LUH$. It is the unique natural comparison satisfying, for every resolving pair $E,G$, with $V=T(E,G)$ and the representative isomorphisms $r,r'$,
$$(\kappa_E\otimes\kappa_G)\,\mu_{q_RE,q_RG}\,U(r_{E,G})=r'_{FE,FG}\,q_S(c_{E,G})\,\kappa_V.$$
Here $T$ is signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and $c:FT(E,G)\cong T(FE,FG)$ is the cochain comparison $c_{u;E,G}$ of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence], the total of the normalized ordinary pure-tensor comparison [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison]: on local generalized pure tensors it sends $s\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. Its inverse sends $(s\otimes x)\otimes(t\otimes y)$ to $st\otimes(x\otimes y)$. The ordinary comparison and its total respect reassociation and signed interchange [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]; termwise $F$ preserves direct sums and all integer differential, shift and interchange signs.

Let $s_{n,K}:U(K[n])\cong(UK)[n]$, and let $t,\alpha,\sigma$ and $t',\alpha',\sigma'$ be the derived comparisons normalized on total models by $(-1)^{bp}$, unsigned reassociation, and $(-1)^{pq}$, respectively. For arbitrary derived $K,H,N$ and all integers $a,b$, the prescribed comparison satisfies
$$t'_{a,b}(s_{a,K}\otimes s_{b,H})\mu_{K[a],H[b]}=\mu_{K,H}[a+b]s_{a+b,K\otimes^LH}U(t_{a,b}),$$
$$\mu_{H,K}U(\sigma_{K,H})=\sigma'_{UK,UH}\mu_{K,H},$$
$$(1\otimes\mu_{H,N})\mu_{K,H\otimes^LN}U(\alpha_{K,H,N})=\alpha'_{UK,UH,UN}(\mu_{K,H}\otimes1)\mu_{K\otimes^LH,N}.$$
These are equations for the canonical comparison with its specified representative normalization, including when both complexes are unbounded. Under $\eta$, $\mu$ is the normalized comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit] (its representative formula is the displayed one, since $\kappa\eta=e$), so the first equation refines the separate-variable shift equations of that node to the composite signed comparisons $t,t'$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to the assumed exact additive module functor $F$. It sends every quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism, and supplies $U=D(F)$, its factorization $\kappa_E:U(q_RE)\cong q_S(FE)$, and all integer shift comparisons $s$. On complexes the shift comparison is the identity in each degree: $F((-1)^nd)=(-1)^nF(d)$. Thus its factorization commutes with shifts, without a boundedness assumption.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), exact functors on all complexes; shift-compatible factorization as in the cited node.

proof.text: The hypotheses are those of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-flat-module-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback]: therefore $F$ preserves flat sheaves and flat-term K-flat complexes. No flatness of $u^{-1}R\to S$ is needed for either assertion. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], this actual scalar-extension pullback is a left adjoint; [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] then shows that it preserves all the direct sums in total tensor complexes, including infinite diagonals. Its additivity preserves every integer scalar, in particular the differential and Koszul signs.

source.place: Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat); sites-modules.tex Tags 05VD (lemma-pullback-flat) and 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules); categories.tex Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact).

proof.text:
Write $\epsilon:Lq_R\to q_SF$ for the natural derived-pullback transformation of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]; its restriction to resolving complexes is $e$. For any complex $A$, take a flat-term K-flat quasi-isomorphism $p:P\to A$ from [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Naturality says
$$q_S(Fp)\epsilon_P=\epsilon_A L(q_Rp).$$
Here $q_S(Fp)$ is invertible by Step 1, $L(q_Rp)$ is invertible because $q_Rp$ is, and $\epsilon_P=e_P$ is invertible by the cited derived-pullback statement. Hence $\epsilon_A$ is invertible for every $A$. The natural isomorphism $\kappa^{-1}\epsilon:Lq_R\cong Uq_R$ descends uniquely through the homotopy-category localization by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to $\eta:L\cong U$. Its inverse descends as well, so this really is an isomorphism. In particular $\kappa_P\eta_{q_RP}=e_P$ on every resolving $P$.

source.place: Tag 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), its natural transformation; Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution). Exactness argument and localization identification supplied explicitly here.

proof.text:
For uniqueness, let $\eta'$ obey the same normalization. Every $A$ admits $p:P\to A$ as in Step 3. Naturality and invertibility of $L(q_Rp),U(q_Rp)$ force
$$\eta'_{q_RA}=U(q_Rp)\eta'_{q_RP}L(q_Rp)^{-1}=\eta_{q_RA}.$$
Every derived object is isomorphic to such an image; alternatively use the equivalence $W_R^{-1}\mathcal P_R\simeq D(R)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Naturality along that isomorphism forces equality at every object. Thus the prescribed normalization determines $\eta$ uniquely.

source.place: Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution); uniqueness under localization on resolving models.

proof.text: For an integer $n$ and a resolving $P$, $P[n]$ is again resolving: its terms are reindexed flat terms, and $T(A,P[n])$ is a shift of $T(A,P)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts], so it is acyclic whenever $A$ is. The shift comparisons for $L$ are those obtained by shifting these resolutions, as specified in [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit]. On $q_RP$ the shift-compatibility square for $\eta$ is therefore the identity of $q_SF(P[n])$ with $q_S(FP)[n]$: both comparisons identify the degree $r$ term with $F(P^{r+n})$ and its differential with $(-1)^nF(d)$. Step 4 extends this square to all derived objects. For a sheaf $M$ in degree zero, Step 3 gives the comparison $\epsilon_{M[0]}:L(M[0])\cong(FM)[0]$; since $U(M[0])$ is represented by $F(M[0])=(FM)[0]$, the equation $\kappa\eta=\epsilon$ identifies exactly the two degree-zero sheaf comparisons. No flatness of $M$ is used.

Let $\mu^L$ be the canonical comparison with the representative formula stated in [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit], and transport it by
$$\mu_{K,H}=(\eta_K\otimes\eta_H)\mu^L_{K,H}\eta_{K\otimes^LH}^{-1}.$$
For resolving $E,G$, [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model] makes $V=T(E,G)$ resolving; Step 2 makes $FE,FG$ resolving over $S$. Thus all of $e_E,e_G,e_V,r,r'$ in that formula are available. Substitute $e_X=\kappa_X\eta_{q_RX}$ for $X=E,G,V$ and use naturality of $\eta$ for $r_{E,G}$. Cancelling these isomorphisms gives precisely
$$(\kappa_E\otimes\kappa_G)\mu_{q_RE,q_RG}U(r_{E,G})=r'_{FE,FG}q_S(c_{E,G})\kappa_V.$$
The cochain map $c$ and its inverse have exactly the local pure-tensor formulas in [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. Hence this is the normalization of the question, not a choice of an abstract tensor isomorphism. The full faithfulness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] implies uniqueness among natural comparisons with these components. This also identifies $\mu$ under $\eta$ with the normalized comparison of the shift-unit node.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), proof by total flat-term K-flat representatives; normalized representative formula of the cited shift-unit node.

proof.text:
Check the two-variable shift equation first on $K=q_RE,H=q_RG$ with resolving $E,G$. By Step 6 and the shift-compatible factorization, cancel $\kappa,r,r'$ throughout; what remains is the chain square between $c_{E[a],G[b]}$ and $c_{E,G}[a+b]$. On the summand corresponding to $x\in E^p$, $y\in G^q$, the stipulated total-shift map multiplies by $(-1)^{bp}$, using the same degree convention over both rings. The two routes both send $s\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to
$$(-1)^{bp}(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y).$$
The normalized maps $c$ are degree-preserving and $F$ preserves multiplication by $-1$, so this is equality of maps of signed total complexes, not only of their graded terms. The total shift maps themselves are the chain isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts], with the chosen order of extracting the two shifts. This proves the first displayed square on resolving pairs for every positive, zero or negative $a,b$.

source.place: more-algebra.tex Tag 0FNH (item-shift-tensor); Tag 07A4 model comparison, explicit homogeneous summand calculation.

proof.text:
For symmetry on a resolving pair, the same cancellation using Step 6 reduces the derived equation to
$$c_{G,E}F(\sigma_{E,G})=\sigma_{FE,FG}c_{E,G}.$$
This is the signed-interchange equation in [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. More explicitly, on degree $(p,q)$ both routes send $s\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(-1)^{pq}(s\otimes y)\otimes(1\otimes x)$: the route through symmetry on the target first gives $(-1)^{pq}(1\otimes y)\otimes(s\otimes x)$, which equals that expression by $S$-balancing. Thus no sign has been dropped in passing from the ordinary pullback comparison to the Koszul comparison.

For associativity choose resolving $E,G,J$. Their pairwise total tensors and both triple totals are resolving by repeated application of [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model]; hence Step 6 applies at every vertex. Substitution of its formula cancels the intermediate representative isomorphisms and leaves
$$(1\otimes c_{G,J})c_{E,T(G,J)}F(\alpha)=\alpha'(c_{E,G}\otimes1)c_{T(E,G),J}.$$
This is the reassociation compatibility asserted in [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. On a local homogeneous generator $s\otimes((x\otimes y)\otimes z)$ both paths give $(s\otimes x)\otimes((1\otimes y)\otimes(1\otimes z))$. Reassociation is unsigned and the total differential agrees on both sides; the cited cochain statement proves equality of chain maps for unbounded complexes as well.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); Tag 07A2 (lemma-tensor-product-K-flat); more-algebra.tex Tag 0FNG, unsigned triple reassociation.

proof.text: Finally these chain calculations imply equations for arbitrary derived inputs. All arrows in each square are natural transformations. For the first two equations, restriction to resolving pairs is faithful by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], so the equalities proved in Steps 7 and 8 hold everywhere. For the associativity equation, choose isomorphisms $q_RE\cong K$, $q_RG\cong H$, $q_RJ\cong N$, possible by the same resolving-category equivalence. Naturality conjugates each side by the same source and target isomorphisms, reducing its value at $(K,H,N)$ to Step 9; cancelling those isomorphisms proves equality. All totalizations used direct sums, whose preservation was proved in Step 2; all resolving and tensor statements cited apply without bounds. This establishes the simultaneous signed shift, symmetry and associativity identities for the specified canonical comparison, including the doubly unbounded case.
